# Tessera: Complete Documentation (llms-full.txt)

> URL: https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/llms-full.txt | Index: https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/llms.txt | Agent Protocol: https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/agents.txt

---

# Tessera: Multi-Agent Coordination for Git

> Run multiple agents in the same Git repository.

Tessera coordinates concurrent AI agents and terminal sessions inside your existing Git repository. Sessions share one checkout, work on independent branches, and merge edits at the AST level.

```ts
// Live Multi-Agent Attribution in src/currency.ts (main):
// [CodeLens] 2 agents concurrently editing this file (main): antigravity-a1b2 · claude-c3d4
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  // [antigravity-a1b2 · L3-L6: Add locale and decimals]
  currency = "USD",
  locale = "en-US",
  decimals = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
// [claude-c3d4 · L10-L14: Add formatCompact helper]
export function formatCompact(cents: number) {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
    style: "currency", currency: "USD", notation: "compact"
  }).format(cents / 100);
}
```

## Why Tessera?

In a standard Git checkout, every open terminal and AI agent shares a single `.git/HEAD` and working directory. Concurrent agents overwrite uncommitted files, switch branches underneath active processes, and collide on local ports. Tessera tracks each session in `.git/tessera` and writes standard Git commits so every agent and terminal tab gets its own branch, Copy-on-Write sandbox, and AST-merged edits inside one folder. [Read Why Tessera? →](/getting-started/why-tessera)

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

### **Semantic Merging**
Tessera parses source files with Tree-sitter to merge functions, imports, class methods, and manifest files at the syntax-tree level rather than line by line.

```ts
// Agent 1 adds `locale`, Agent 2 adds `decimals` to the same signature:
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  currency: string = "USD",
  locale: string = "en-US",
  decimals: number = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
```

### **Session Isolation**
Each terminal tab and agent session can switch to its own branch without changing `.git/HEAD` for the rest of your workspace. Edits on the same branch combine automatically on disk, while edits on separate branches stay completely isolated.

```bash
# Terminal 1 works on feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing

# Terminal 2 works on feat/faq at the same time
tes switch feat/faq
```

### **Instant Sandboxes**
Run builds, tests, and dev servers on any branch without reinstalling dependencies. Tessera clones `node_modules`, `target`, and `.venv` using filesystem copy-on-write, assigns each session a `TES_PORT` slot (enable full dev-server port isolation with `tes config set port_isolation true` or `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1`; defaults to `false`), and isolates locally configured test database URLs.

```bash
# Run builds or dev servers in isolated Copy-on-Write branch sandboxes
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm test
```

## Work in Parallel

Run multiple agents on the same branch, split features across branches, or run two dev servers side by side from a single checkout.

### 1. Multiple Agents

```bash
# Initialize Tessera and install AI editor rules
tes init

# Prompt two AI agents in parallel:
# Tab 1: "On branch feat/pricing, build PricingCalculator.vue and add it to App.vue"
# Tab 2: "On branch feat/faq, build TestimonialsFaq.vue and add it to App.vue"

# Check live agent sessions and claimed files
tes radar
```

### 2. Per-Terminal Branches

```bash
# Enable (tes:<branch>) in your shell prompt and opt into dev-server port isolation
tes env --install
tes config set port_isolation true

# Terminal 1: run feat/pricing on port 3100
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev

# Terminal 2: run feat/faq on port 3200
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
```

### 3. Branch Merging

```bash
# Inspect branch diffs against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
tes diff -b feat/faq

# Merge both branches into main using 3-way AST merge
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"

# Push to remote
tes push
```

---

# TL;DR

Tessera coordinates multiple AI agents and terminal sessions in the same Git checkout on separate branches or the same branch. Each session gets its own branch state, Copy-on-Write sandbox, and `TES_PORT` slot inside one repository folder (enable automatic dev-server port isolation with `tes config set port_isolation true` or `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1`; it defaults to `false`). `tes init` writes instruction and hook files (Antigravity by default, plus auto-detected Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro, OpenCode, Codex, and VS Code, or `--harness all`) so your agents use `tes` automatically. Pass `tes init --local` on mixed teams to add installed rule files to `.git/info/exclude`.

## Install

**macOS, Linux, and BSD:**

```bash
curl -fsSL https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.sh | sh
tes init
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
irm https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.ps1 | iex
tes init
```

# Getting Started

Tessera coordinates multiple AI coding agents and terminal sessions inside an existing Git repository. This guide covers installing the `tes` CLI, initializing a repository, and running a multi-branch workflow.

## Prerequisites

- **OS**: macOS, Linux, Windows, FreeBSD, or OpenBSD
- **Git**: Standard Git 2.23+

## Installation

Install the `tes` CLI on **macOS, Linux, or BSD**:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.sh | sh
tes --version
```

Or on **Windows (PowerShell)**:

```powershell
irm https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.ps1 | iex
tes --version
```

For shell integration, prebuilt binaries, and editor setup details, see the [Installation Guide](/getting-started/installation).

## Initializing Your Project

Navigate to any project directory and run `tes init`:

```bash
tes init
```

This creates `.git/tessera`, installs Git sync hooks (`post-commit`, `post-merge`, and `post-checkout`), and installs workspace rules for your AI coding editors (Antigravity by default, plus auto-detected Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro, OpenCode, Codex, and VS Code, or specify `--harness all|<list>`). Pass `tes init --local` on mixed teams to exclude installed rule files via `.git/info/exclude`.

> **Note:** If the directory is not yet a Git repository, `tes init` runs `git init` and creates an initial commit from your existing files before setting up Tessera.

## Your First Workflow

Switch your current terminal tab to a feature branch, run your tests, and merge your work:

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
npm test
tes status
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator"
```

## What Each Command Does

```bash
tes init
```

- Sets up `.git/tessera` and Git sync hooks (`.git/hooks/post-commit`, `post-merge`, and `post-checkout`) inside your existing Git repository
- Installs instruction rules for Antigravity (`.agents/rules/tessera.md`) by default plus auto-detected AI editors (`CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/settings.json`, `.cursor/rules/tessera.mdc`, `AGENTS.md`, and more; use `--harness all` to install all, or `--local` to add them to `.git/info/exclude`)

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
```

- Binds your current terminal tab to the `feat/pricing` branch (creating it from `HEAD` if it does not exist yet)
- Prepares a Copy-on-Write sandbox for `feat/pricing` that shares your existing `node_modules`, `target`, or `.venv`

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator"
```

- Merges `feat/pricing` into `main` using Tessera's 3-way AST merge engine
- Updates your working directory on `main`

## Working in a Single Folder

In a standard Git checkout, every terminal tab and AI agent shares `.git/HEAD` and the working tree on disk. Tessera isolates each session inside a **single repository folder** with its own branch state and `TES_PORT` slot. When running concurrent dev servers on separate branches, enable `port_isolation` (defaults to `false`) with `tes config set port_isolation true` or `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1`:

```bash
# Enable automatic dev-server port isolation (defaults to false)
tes config set port_isolation true

# Terminal 1 works on feat/pricing (assigned port 3100)
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev

# Terminal 2 works on feat/faq in the same folder (assigned port 3200)
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
```

When you prompt an AI agent in your editor, you do not need to mention `tes` in your prompt:

```text
On branch feat/pricing, create PricingCalculator.vue and add it to src/App.vue.
```

The workspace rules installed by `tes init` instruct the agent to claim the branch, isolate its edits, verify the build in its branch sandbox, and commit.

## Next Steps

- [Why Tessera?](/getting-started/why-tessera) - Understand the core problems Tessera solves for parallel AI agents
- [Installation](/getting-started/installation) - Set up `(tes:<branch>)` in your terminal prompt and tab completion
- [Your First Workflow](/getting-started/first-workflow) - Walk through a multi-agent example step by step
- [Guides](/guides/) - Learn about multi-agent workflows, dev servers, conflicts, and editor integration

# Why Tessera?

A Git checkout has a single `.git/HEAD` pointer and a single working tree on disk. Every terminal tab, background process, and AI coding agent opened in a project directory reads and writes that shared state:

1. **Working tree and branch overwrites**: If two agents edit `src/App.vue` concurrently, the second save overwrites the first agent's lines, or an agent sees unfamiliar edits on disk and reverts them. Switching branches to test a task changes `.git/HEAD` underneath your editor, running dev servers, and every other open terminal.
2. **Line-based merge conflicts**: Concurrent tasks frequently modify adjacent lines in shared files, such as adding imports at the top of a module, registering routes or components, or updating dependencies in `package.json` and lockfiles. Line-based diffing flags these compatible additions as conflicts.
3. **Port and cache collisions**: Running test suites or dev servers for two tasks at the same time collides on hardcoded ports (`localhost:3000`), build caches (`target/`, `node_modules/`), and local test databases.

## One Folder, Isolated Sessions

Tessera lets multiple AI agents and terminal tabs work in the **same repository folder** at the same time, either on separate branches or on the same branch.

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

When an agent claims a branch like `feat/pricing`, Tessera isolates that session inside `.git/tessera/` without changing `.git/HEAD` for the rest of your workspace. Concurrent agents can edit `src/App.vue` on their own branches in `~/acme-web` at the same time without touching each other's uncommitted files.

When you want to build, test, or preview a branch, `tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run dev` executes inside a Copy-on-Write sandbox. It clones your existing `node_modules`, `target`, or `.venv` directories (including monorepo workspace symlinks), preserves your untracked `.env*` secrets and `.gitignore`d local files (such as local SQLite databases or `.dev.vars`), assigns each branch its own `TES_PORT` slot (`3100`, `3200`; enable full dev-server `PORT` isolation and POSIX port shims with `tes config set port_isolation true`, which defaults to `false`), and isolates locally configured `DATABASE_URL` / `TEST_DATABASE_URL` database names with `_slot_<N>` so you can run multiple branches side by side.

## Structural Merging Across Code, Configs, and Lockfiles

When you run `tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main`, Tessera merges changes using language-aware parsers and format-preserving drivers with fail-safe fallbacks:

- **Tree-sitter AST merging (6 grammars + SFCs)**: Uses Tree-sitter grammars for **Rust** (`.rs`), **TypeScript** (`.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`), **TSX** (`.tsx`), **JavaScript / JSX** (`.js`, `.jsx`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`), **Python** (`.py`, `.pyi`), and **Go** (`.go`), plus `<script>` blocks in **Vue** and **Svelte** single-file components (SFCs), to merge functions, class and `impl` methods, imports, and signatures structurally.
- **Format-preserving manifest and lockfile drivers**: Structurally merges `Cargo.toml`, `Cargo.lock`, `*.toml`, and `*.json` (including `package.json`) by key and stanza while preserving formatting and flagging conflicting scalar values cleanly.
- **Fail-safe fallback and binary/symlink/submodule safety**: Other languages and text formats fall back to structural and strict line 3-way diff3 merging. Binary files, tracked symbolic links (`120000`), and Git submodule gitlinks (`160000`) are never text-merged blindly and instead preserve modes or record first-class conflicts when both sides diverge.

## Editing on the Same Branch

When two agents work directly on `main` at the same time, Tessera runs a 3-way structural merge on disk whenever either agent saves a file.

```text
[Workflow: Same-Branch AST Merging on main]
1. Prompt on main   -> Agent 1 ("Add locale") & Agent 2 ("Add decimals") target src/currency.ts
2. Concurrent Edits -> Both agents save directly on main (no file locks)
3. Tree-sitter AST  -> Parses FunctionDecl -> merges ParamNode[1] (locale) + ParamNode[2] (decimals)
4. Unified on Disk  -> Both edits preserved in src/currency.ts with zero overwrites
```

If one agent updates `formatCurrency()` while another adds `formatCompact()` in `src/currency.ts`, both edits are preserved on disk. In VS Code and Cursor, the Tessera extension highlights each agent's lines so you can see which session owns each change.

## Git Compatibility

Tessera stores session state locally in `.git/tessera/` with no external server. Every `tes commit` or `tes merge` writes standard Git blobs, trees, and commits directly into `.git/objects/` and `refs/heads/*`, so `git push`, GitHub pull requests, and CI pipelines work without changes.

# Installation

This guide covers installing the `tes` CLI, enabling shell prompt integration, and configuring your AI coding editors.

## Requirements

Tessera is lightweight and self-contained:

- **OS**: macOS (APFS), Linux (Btrfs / XFS / bcachefs / ext4), FreeBSD, OpenBSD, or Windows (WSL2 and native Windows with PowerShell / Windows Terminal)
- **Git**: Standard Git 2.23+

> [!INFO]
> On macOS (APFS) and Linux (Btrfs / XFS / bcachefs), Tessera uses native Copy-on-Write filesystem clones (`clonefile` and `FICLONE`) to duplicate `node_modules` and `target` directories in milliseconds without using extra disk space. On ext4, FreeBSD, OpenBSD, and Windows, Tessera automatically falls back to portable recursive sandbox cloning.

## Installing the CLI

### macOS, Linux, and BSD

Install `tes` on macOS (Apple Silicon & Intel), Linux (`x86_64` & `ARM64`, glibc & musl), FreeBSD, or OpenBSD:

```bash
curl -fsSL https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.sh | sh
```

### Windows (PowerShell)

Install `tes.exe` on Windows (`x86_64` and `ARM64`) using PowerShell:

```powershell
irm https://tessera.getlunaris.dev/install.ps1 | iex
```

The Windows installer verifies the SHA-256 checksum, extracts `tes.exe` into `$HOME\.local\bin`, and adds it to your user `Path`.

### Prebuilt Binaries

You can also download prebuilt archives directly from GitHub Releases:

| Platform                           | Architecture                            | Release Archive                                                                  |
| ---------------------------------- | --------------------------------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| **macOS**                          | Apple Silicon (`arm64`)                 | [`tes-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) |
| **macOS**                          | Intel (`x86_64`)                        | [`tes-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-apple-darwin.tar.gz) |
| **Linux**                          | `x86_64` (static musl / glibc)          | [`tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz) / [`tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) |
| **Linux**                          | `ARM64` (`aarch64` static musl / glibc) | [`tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-musl.tar.gz) / [`tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu.tar.gz) |
| **Windows**                        | `x86_64` (MSVC)                         | [`tes-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) |
| **Windows**                        | `ARM64` (MSVC)                          | [`tes-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-aarch64-pc-windows-msvc.zip) |
| **FreeBSD**                        | `x86_64`                                | [`tes-x86_64-unknown-freebsd.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-freebsd.tar.gz) |
| **OpenBSD**                        | `x86_64`                                | [`tes-x86_64-unknown-openbsd.tar.gz`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tes-x86_64-unknown-openbsd.tar.gz) |
| **VS Code & VS Code-based IDEs**   | Universal `.vsix`                       | [`tessera-vscode.vsix`](https://github.com/tessera-vcs/tessera/releases/latest/download/tessera-vscode.vsix) |

Verify the installation:

```bash
tes --version
```

## Shell Integration

Each terminal tab can switch branches independently, so it helps to show the active branch in your prompt:

```text
~/code/my-app main (tes:feat/pricing) ❯
```

### Automatic Setup

Run `tes env --install` once to configure your shell profiles (`~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`, `~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, `~/.mkshrc`, `~/.tcshrc`, `~/.cshrc`, Fish's `config.fish`, and PowerShell's `$PROFILE` on Windows) automatically:

```bash
tes env --install
```

Open a new terminal tab (or reload your shell profile) to activate the prompt indicator, environment variable sync, and tab completion.

### Shell Capabilities

| Shell | Prompt & Env Sync | Dynamic `<TAB>` Completion | Automatic Branch Sandbox Command Routing |
| ----- | ----------------- | -------------------------- | ---------------------------------------- |
| **Zsh** (`--zsh`) | Yes | Yes | Yes (`preexec` / `precmd`) |
| **Bash** (`--bash`) | Yes | Yes | Yes (`DEBUG` trap / `PROMPT_COMMAND`) |
| **Fish** (`--fish`) | Yes | Yes | Yes (`fish_preexec` / `fish_prompt`) |
| **PowerShell** (`--pwsh`) | Yes | Yes | Use `tes exec [-b <branch>] -- <cmd>` |
| **POSIX `sh` / `dash` / `ksh` / `mksh` / `oksh` / `yash`** (`--sh`) | Yes | No | Use `tes exec [-b <branch>] -- <cmd>` |
| **`tcsh` / BSD `csh`** (`--tcsh`) | Yes | No | Use `tes exec [-b <branch>] -- <cmd>` |
| **Nushell** (`--nu`) | Yes | No | Use `tes exec [-b <branch>] -- <cmd>` |
| **Elvish** (`--elvish`) | Yes | No | Use `tes exec [-b <branch>] -- <cmd>` |

> [!INFO]
> Environment variables (`TES_PORT`, `PORT` when `port_isolation = true`, `TES_BRANCH`, `TES_DB_NAME`, and locally configured `DATABASE_URL`) work cross-platform across macOS, Linux, BSD, and Windows. Executable CLI port-wrapper shims (`TES_SHIM_BIN`) are POSIX-only (macOS, Linux, BSD, and WSL).

### Manual Shell Setup

If you prefer to configure your shell manually, add the line matching your shell:

**Zsh (`~/.zshrc`)** (Powerlevel10k, Oh My Zsh, Starship, and default Zsh)

```bash
eval "$(tes env --zsh)"
```

**Bash (`~/.bashrc` or `~/.bash_profile`)** (Bash 3.2+ and 5.x, Starship, Oh My Bash, and default Bash)

```bash
eval "$(tes env --bash)"
```

**Fish (`~/.config/fish/config.fish`)** (Tide, Starship, Hydro, and default Fish)

```bash
tes env --fish | source
```

**POSIX `sh` / `dash` / `ksh` / `mksh` / `oksh` / `yash` (`~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, or `~/.mkshrc`)**

```bash
eval "$(tes env --sh)"
```

**`tcsh` / BSD `csh` (`~/.tcshrc` or `~/.cshrc`)**

```bash
eval "`tes env --tcsh`"
```

**Nushell (`~/.config/nushell/config.nu`)**

```bash
tes env --nu | save -f ~/.config/nushell/tes.nu
source ~/.config/nushell/tes.nu
```

**Elvish (`~/.config/elvish/rc.elv`)**

```bash
tes env --elvish >> ~/.config/elvish/rc.elv
```

**PowerShell (`$PROFILE`)**

```powershell
Invoke-Expression (& tes env --pwsh)
```

## Initializing a Repository

Inside any project directory, run:

```bash
tes init
```

By default, `tes init` installs `.agents/rules/tessera.md` (Antigravity), Git sync hooks (`.git/hooks/post-commit`, `post-merge`, and `post-checkout`), and auto-detected integrations for Claude Code, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro, OpenCode, Codex, and VS Code when their repository files or environment variables are present. To target specific editors or install all of them, pass `--harness`:

```bash
tes init --harness antigravity
tes init --harness claude
tes init --harness cursor
tes init --harness windsurf
tes init --harness kiro
tes init --harness opencode
tes init --harness codex
tes init --harness vscode
tes init --harness all
```

On mixed teams where not every contributor uses Tessera, pass `--local` so installed agent rule and harness files are added to `.git/info/exclude` instead of appearing as untracked files in `git status`:

```bash
tes init --local
tes init --local --harness claude,cursor
```

## Upgrading Tessera

Update `tes` in place at any time with SHA-256 verification and atomic binary replacement:

```bash
# check if a newer release is available
tes upgrade --check

# upgrade to the latest release (also works as `tes update`, `tes --upgrade`, or `tes --update`)
tes upgrade
```

## Uninstalling Tessera

### 1. Remove Shell Integration

If you configured shell prompt integration (`tes env --install`), remove the `tes env` line from your shell profile:

- **Zsh (`~/.zshrc`)**: remove `eval "$(tes env --zsh 2>/dev/null)"`
- **Bash (`~/.bashrc`, `~/.bash_profile`)**: remove `eval "$(tes env --bash 2>/dev/null)"`
- **POSIX `sh` (`~/.profile`, `~/.kshrc`, `~/.mkshrc`)**: remove `eval "$(tes env --sh 2>/dev/null)"`
- **Fish (`~/.config/fish/config.fish`)**: remove `tes env --fish 2>/dev/null | source`
- **`tcsh` / `csh` (`~/.tcshrc`, `~/.cshrc`)**: remove `` eval "`tes env --tcsh`" ``
- **PowerShell (`$PROFILE`)**: remove `Invoke-Expression (& tes env --pwsh)`

### 2. Delete the CLI Binary

**macOS, Linux, and BSD:**

```bash
rm -f ~/.local/bin/tes
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**

```powershell
Remove-Item -Force "$HOME\.local\bin\tes.exe"
```

### 3. Clean Up Repository State (Optional)

Inside any repository where you ran `tes init`, Tessera stores its metadata and sandboxes in `.git/tessera` (and Git hooks that automatically no-op when `tes` is not installed). To remove the local Tessera state from a repository, delete `.git/tessera`.

# Your First Workflow

In this guide, you will initialize Tessera in a project, work across two feature branches in parallel, and merge both branches back into `main`.

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

## 1. Initialize the Repository

Start by running `tes init` in your project root (pass `tes init --local` on mixed teams to add installed agent rule files to `.git/info/exclude`):

```bash
tes init
```

If you have not already enabled shell prompt integration, run:

```bash
tes env --install
```

If you plan to run multiple dev servers side by side on separate branches, enable automatic port isolation (`port_isolation` defaults to `false`):

```bash
tes config set port_isolation true
```

## 2. Work on Two Branches in Parallel

You can work on multiple branches at the same time by prompting two AI agent tabs or opening two terminal tabs.

### Option A: Prompt Two AI Agents

Open two AI agent chat tabs in your editor and give each one a task on its own branch:

- **Tab 1**: *"On branch `feat/pricing`, create `src/components/PricingCalculator.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*
- **Tab 2**: *"On branch `feat/faq`, create `src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*

### Option B: Use Two Terminal Tabs

Or open two terminal tabs in the same repository and switch each terminal to its own branch:

**Terminal 1:**

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
```

**Terminal 2:**

```bash
tes switch feat/faq
```

> **Tip:** Each terminal tab remembers its own branch without changing `.git/HEAD` for your editor or other terminals.

## 3. Inspect Live Sessions and Changes

At any point, you can view active agent sessions, modified files, and diffs:

```bash
# See all active agent and terminal sessions
tes radar

# List all branches in the repository
tes branch

# View modified files in the current session or branch
tes status

# Compare a specific branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
tes diff -b feat/faq
```

### Command Summary

**`tes radar`**
- Shows every active AI agent or terminal session
- Displays each session's target branch, assigned port (`:3100`, `:3200`), and claimed files

**`tes status`**
- **Staged / Session Changes**: Files recorded in the current session (`M`, `A`, `D`)
- **Unstaged Changes**: Working tree edits on disk not yet reconciled
- **Committed on Branch**: Files committed on the feature branch ahead of `main`

**`tes diff -b <branch>`**
- Shows a unified diff comparing `<branch>` against `main` without switching your editor branch

## 4. Merge Both Branches into `main`

When both features are ready, combine them into `main` with a single command:

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator and faq"
```

Even if both `feat/pricing` and `feat/faq` added imports and components to `src/App.vue`, Tessera's 3-way AST merge engine combines both sets of imports and template blocks without conflict markers.

## Key Concepts

### 1. Per-Session Branches

In standard Git, `git checkout feat/pricing` switches the entire folder for every open terminal and AI agent. In Tessera:

- `tes switch feat/pricing` binds only the **current terminal session** to `feat/pricing`.
- `tes claim --branch feat/pricing ...` binds only that **AI agent session** to `feat/pricing`.
- Clicking the branch name in the IDE status bar (or running `tes switch feat/pricing --editor`) switches your **editor working tree** (`repo_root`) so your file explorer displays `feat/pricing`.

### 2. Branch Sandboxes

When you run commands in a switched terminal or via `tes exec -b <branch> -- <cmd>`, Tessera runs the command inside a Copy-on-Write sandbox for that branch:

```bash
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm run build
```

Both commands reuse your existing `node_modules` (or `target` / `.venv`).

### 3. Checkpoints and Undo

Every operation in Tessera is recorded in an operation log inside `.git/tessera`. If an agent makes an unwanted change or you want to roll back a merge, run:

```bash
tes undo
```

- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - Managing terminal branches, editor branches, and merges
- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Using the branch graph and status bar switcher in VS Code

# Agents

After running `tes init`, editors and CLI harnesses (Antigravity, Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro, and OpenCode) coordinate edits automatically inside the repository.

## Automatic Coordination

You do not need to change how you prompt your AI agents or manually manage locks. The workspace rules installed by `tes init` instruct each agent to run four commands:

```text
[Workflow: How Agents Coordinate Automatically]
1. Claim Task        -> tes claim [--branch <branch>] [--from <base>] --intent "<goal>" <files...>
2. Reconcile Edits   -> tes hook post-tool --path <files...> (3-way AST merge on save)
3. Verify in Sandbox -> tes exec -- npm run build            (CoW sandbox on isolated port)
4. Commit to Git     -> tes commit -m "..." / tes merge      (standard Git commit on branch)
```

1. **Claim the task (`tes claim`)**: Before editing files, the agent declares what it is working on, which files it will touch, and (optionally) which branch and base branch it is targeting:
   ```bash
   tes claim --branch feat/pricing --intent "Add pricing calculator" src/components/PricingCalculator.vue src/App.vue
   ```
2. **Reconcile edits (`tes hook post-tool`)**: Immediately after modifying files, the agent reconciles its edits:
   ```bash
   tes hook post-tool --path src/components/PricingCalculator.vue src/App.vue
   ```
3. **Verify in a sandbox (`tes exec`)**: To run a compiler, type-checker, or test suite, the agent executes inside its branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox:
   ```bash
   tes exec -- npm run build
   ```
4. **Commit (`tes commit` / `tes merge`)**: When finished, the agent commits its changes cleanly onto its target branch:
   ```bash
   tes commit -m "feat(pricing): add pricing calculator"
   ```

## Same Branch vs. Separate Branches

### Same Branch

When two agents work on the **same branch** (for example, both editing on `main`), Tessera combines their edits automatically using 3-way AST merging:

- **Functions and Methods**: Two agents can add or edit different functions, or add methods to the same `class` or `impl` block, in the same file.
- **Imports and Parameters**: Both agents can add imports to the top of a file or add parameters to the same function signature.
- **Vue and Svelte Components**: Concurrent edits to `<script setup>`, `<template>`, and `<style scoped>` blocks merge cleanly.
- **Manifests and Lockfiles**: Concurrent additions to `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` are merged structurally.

> **Dirty Claim Auto-Isolation (`auto_isolate_dirty_claims`):** By default (`auto_isolate_dirty_claims = true`), if a fresh session runs `tes claim` *without* `--branch` on a file that already has uncommitted changes from you or another session, Tessera automatically isolates that new session onto `agent/<session_id>` so it does not mix edits into in-progress work. To collaborate directly on the same branch, pass `--branch <branch>` explicitly (for example, `tes claim --branch main --intent "..." src/currency.ts`), or disable auto-isolation with `tes config set auto_isolate_dirty_claims false`.

### Separate Branches

When you ask Agent 1 to work on `feat/pricing` and Agent 2 to work on `feat/faq`, both agents may touch shared files like `src/App.vue` or `index.html` at the same time.

Tessera keeps each branch isolated:
- Changes made on `feat/pricing` never leak into `feat/faq`'s sandbox or commit tree.
- Agents on different branches edit independent trees and do not conflict while building their features.
- When both agents finish, you can inspect each branch independently or merge both into `main` with `tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main`.

## Status and Diffs

Check modified files in your current session or branch with `tes status`:

```bash
tes status
```

`tes status` groups files into sections:
- **Staged / Session Changes**: Changes recorded in the active session (`M`, `A`, `D`)
- **Peer Session Changes on `<branch>`**: Files modified by other concurrent sessions on the same branch
- **Unstaged Changes**: Working tree edits on disk not yet claimed by any session
- **Committed on `<branch>`**: Files committed on the current feature branch ahead of `main`

Use `tes diff` to view line-by-line diffs:

```bash
# View all changes in the current session or working tree
tes diff

# View only staged session changes
tes diff --staged

# View changes for a single file
tes diff src/App.vue

# Compare any branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
```

## Live Sessions

To see all active agents and terminal sessions in real time, run:

```bash
tes radar
```

`tes radar` shows each session's ID, assigned port slot, target branch, task intent, and modified files.

- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - Switching and merging branches
- [Sandboxes](/guides/running-tests-and-servers) - Running builds and dev servers in branch sandboxes
- [Examples](/examples/) - Step-by-step walkthroughs

# Branches

In standard Git, all open terminals and editor windows share a single `.git/HEAD`. Running `git checkout feat/pricing` in one terminal switches the branch underneath every other open terminal and AI agent.

Tessera tracks **per-terminal branches**, **per-agent branches**, and your **editor branch** independently.

```text
[Architecture: Editor, Terminal & Agent Branches in One Folder]
- Editor Working Tree : .git/HEAD stays on main in VS Code and VS Code-based IDEs
- Terminal Tabs       : tes switch feat/pricing (:3100) | tes switch feat/faq (:3200)
- Agent Branches      : tes claim --branch isolates agent edits inside .git/tessera/
- Switch or Merge     : tes switch <branch> --editor  OR  tes merge ... --into main
```

## Switching Branches

When shell integration is enabled (`tes env --install`), each terminal tab has its own session and can switch branches independently:

```bash
# Terminal 1
tes switch feat/pricing

# Terminal 2
tes switch feat/faq
```

If the target branch does not exist yet, Tessera creates it automatically from `HEAD` (or from your session's current branch if that tab is already on a feature branch). To branch off a specific parent branch explicitly, pass `--from <base-branch>` or use `tes switch -b <new-branch> <base-branch>`:

```bash
tes switch -b feat/pricing-tiers feat/pricing
# or
tes switch feat/pricing-tiers --from feat/pricing
```

In a switched terminal tab:
- Your shell prompt displays `(tes:feat/pricing)` so you always see which branch that tab is on.
- In Zsh, Bash, and Fish, commands you run in that terminal (`npm test`, `npm run build`, `npm run dev`, `cargo test`) execute automatically inside that branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox while your terminal prompt stays in your project folder (in other shells, run `tes exec -- <command>`).
- Other open terminals and your code editor remain untouched.

## Switching the Editor Branch

When you want your IDE file explorer and language server to display a different branch's files in your main repository folder, switch the editor branch:

- **In VS Code or any VS Code-based IDE**: Click the branch name in the bottom-left status bar and select the branch from the dropdown.
- **From the CLI**: Pass `--editor` (or `-e`) to `tes switch`:

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing --editor
```

Switching the editor branch updates your repository working tree and `.git/HEAD` while keeping any open terminal tabs pinned to their own branches.

## Assigning an Agent to a Branch

To have an AI agent build a feature on a specific branch without switching your editor away from `main`, name the branch in your prompt:

> *"On branch `feat/faq`, create `src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue` and add it to `src/App.vue`."*

The agent claims the branch automatically:

```bash
tes claim --branch feat/faq --intent "Add Testimonials and FAQ section" src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue src/App.vue
```

To have an agent create a new branch stacked on top of an existing feature branch, specify the parent branch in your prompt (for example, *"Branch off `feat/pricing` into `feat/pricing-tiers`..."*). The agent passes `--from feat/pricing` when claiming or switching:

```bash
tes claim --branch feat/pricing-tiers --from feat/pricing --intent "Add enterprise pricing tier" src/components/PricingCalculator.vue
```

When the agent finishes and commits onto `feat/faq`, your `main` working tree remains clean.

## Listing Branches

View all branches in the repository and see which branch your current terminal session is using:

```bash
tes branch
```

Pass `--json` to inspect commit hashes, assigned ports, active sessions, and modified files ahead of `main`:

```bash
tes branch --json
```

## Merging Branches

Combine one or more feature branches into `main` (or any target branch) using `tes merge --into`:

```bash
# Merge a single branch into main
tes merge feat/pricing --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator"

# Merge multiple branches into main at once
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

During `tes merge`, Tessera merges unchanged directories without reading file blobs, detects renamed files across directories, renumbers colliding sequential SQL migrations, merges `package.json`, `Cargo.toml`, and `Cargo.lock` dependencies structurally, and combines concurrent AST changes with Tree-sitter.

## Pushing to Remotes

Commit any pending session changes and push a branch to your Git remote (`origin`):

```bash
tes push
tes push -u origin feat/pricing
```

## See Also

- [Sandboxes](/guides/running-tests-and-servers) - Running builds and dev servers across branches
- [Conflicts](/guides/conflict-resolution) - Handling conflicts and rolling back merges
- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Switching and merging branches in VS Code

# Sandboxes

Tessera creates Copy-on-Write branch sandboxes that reuse your existing dependencies, preserve your untracked `.env*` secrets and `.gitignore`d files, assign each branch its own `TES_PORT` slot (`3100`, `3200`; enable full dev-server `PORT` isolation via `tes config set port_isolation true`, which defaults to `false`), and isolate locally configured test database URLs.

## Running Commands

With shell integration enabled (`tes env --install`), switch a terminal tab to any branch and run your test or build commands directly:

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
npm test
npm run build
```

Open a second terminal tab, switch it to another branch, and run tests there at the same time:

```bash
tes switch feat/faq
npm test
```

Each terminal tab executes against its own branch's files and dependencies without interfering with other tabs.

## Running Dev Servers

To preview two feature branches in your browser at the same time with automatic port isolation, enable `port_isolation`:

```bash
tes config set port_isolation true
```

Then switch each terminal tab to its branch and start your dev server:

**Terminal 1:**

```bash
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev
# TES_PORT=3100
```

**Terminal 2:**

```bash
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
# TES_PORT=3200
```

Or run them explicitly with `tes exec -b <branch>`:

```bash
# Terminal 1
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run dev -- --port 3100

# Terminal 2
tes exec -b feat/faq -- npm run dev -- --port 3200
```

## One-Off Commands

Use `tes exec` to run a command inside a branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox without switching your terminal tab:

```bash
# Run on the current session's branch
tes exec -- npm run build

# Run on a specific branch
tes exec -b feat/pricing -- npm run build
tes exec -b feat/faq -- ./node_modules/.bin/vue-tsc -b
```

When `tes exec` runs:
1. Tessera materializes the branch's committed files plus any uncommitted changes for that branch into its sandbox.
2. Dependency and build cache directories (`node_modules`, `target`, `.venv`, `vendor`) are cloned via Copy-on-Write.
3. `<sandbox>/node_modules/.bin`, `<sandbox>/.venv/bin`, and `<sandbox>/vendor/bin` are prepended to `PATH`.
4. Any new or modified source files generated by the command (such as codegen output or lockfile updates) are captured back into the branch state.

## Dependency Caches

Tessera clones and synchronizes default dependency and build caches across major ecosystems (`cow_cache_dirs`):

| Ecosystem | Default Cached Directories |
|-----------|----------------------------|
| **JavaScript / TypeScript** | `node_modules`, `.pnpm-store`, `.turbo`, `.next`, `.nuxt`, `.svelte-kit`, `dist`, `build` |
| **Rust** | `target` (plus `CARGO_TARGET_DIR` when `Cargo.toml` is present) |
| **Python** | `.venv`, `venv`, `__pycache__`, `.pytest_cache`, `.mypy_cache`, `.ruff_cache` |
| **Go / PHP / Ruby** | `vendor` |
| **Elixir / Erlang** | `_build`, `deps` |
| **JVM / Swift / C++** | `.gradle`, `.build`, `cmake-build-debug`, `cmake-build-release` |
| **Zig / Dart** | `.zig-cache`, `zig-out`, `.dart_tool` |

To add extra project-specific cache folders (such as `.nx`, `.vite`, or `.tox`), run `tes config add-cache-dir <dir...>`.

> **Tip:** If you run `npm install` in your project root *after* a branch sandbox was already created, Tessera syncs the newly installed `node_modules` into the branch sandbox on the next `tes exec` run.

## Environment Variables and Database Isolation

Each session slot (`1`, `2`, `3`, ...) receives non-overlapping environment variables:

| Variable | Slot 1 | Slot 2 | Description |
|----------|--------|--------|-------------|
| `TES_PORT` | `3100` | `3200` | Always exported; calculated as `base_port + (slot * port_stride)` |
| `PORT` (plus framework vars) | `3100` | `3200` | Exported when `port_isolation = true` or `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1` (defaults to `false`) |
| `TES_BRANCH` | `feat/pricing` | `feat/faq` | Target branch name for the session |
| `TES_DB_NAME` | `test_slot_1` | `test_slot_2` | Isolated database name identifier for integration tests |
| `DATABASE_URL` / `TEST_DATABASE_URL` | `.../<db>_slot_1` | `.../<db>_slot_2` | Suffixed only when a local network database URL is already configured |

### How `DATABASE_URL` Isolation Works

Tessera does **not** fabricate a fake `DATABASE_URL` or SQLite URL when none is configured:

- **Local network databases**: If `DATABASE_URL` or `TEST_DATABASE_URL` is set in the environment or in `.env.development.local`, `.env.local`, `.env.development`, or `.env` and points to a local database host (`localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `[::1]`, `0.0.0.0`, `host.docker.internal`, or `*.localhost`), Tessera appends `_slot_<N>` to the database name (for example, `postgres://localhost:5432/myapp` becomes `postgres://localhost:5432/myapp_slot_1`), preserving query parameters and fragments and avoiding double-suffixing.
- **SQLite, file-based, and remote/cloud databases**: File-based URLs (`sqlite:`, `sqlite3:`, `sqlite+*:`, `file:`, `duckdb:`, `*.db`, `*.sqlite*`, `:memory:`), Redis/HTTP/WebSocket URLs, and remote or cloud database URLs (such as Neon, Supabase, or RDS) are left completely untouched.

> **Platform Note:** Environment variable isolation works across macOS, Linux, BSD, and Windows. Executable CLI port-wrapper shims (`TES_SHIM_BIN`, used when `port_isolation = true`) are POSIX-only (macOS, Linux, BSD, and WSL).

To customize `base_port`, `port_stride`, `port_isolation`, `cow_cache_dirs`, or custom environment variable templates, see the [Configuration Guide](/guides/configuration).

---

# Conflicts

Tessera combines concurrent edits to separate functions, imports, class methods, and manifest entries using 3-way Tree-sitter AST merging and manifest drivers.

A conflict occurs when two sessions or branches modify the same statement or expression in incompatible ways, such as rewriting the same heading or return expression to different values.

## Resolving in the Editor

When a merge conflict occurs while using the Tessera IDE extension (in VS Code, Antigravity, Cursor, Windsurf, Kiro, or VSCodium):

1. Tessera writes standard Git conflict markers (`<<<<<<<`, `=======`, `>>>>>>>`) into the file.
2. The extension opens the conflicted file in your editor and jumps to the `<<<<<<<` line.
3. Edit the file to keep the code you want, remove the conflict markers, and save (`Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S`).
4. As soon as the file is saved without conflict markers, Tessera resolves the conflict, updates the working tree and sandbox, and records the resolution on the active branch.

You can also click **`N Conflicts`** in the bottom status bar (or run **`Tessera: Open Conflict Resolver`**) to inspect competing agent intents, `Base` / `Ours` / `Theirs` snippets, and verification `diagnostics`, edit the `AST-Union Preview`, click **`Open in Editor`**, or resolve with **`Accept AST-Union`**, **`Accept Ours`**, **`Accept Theirs`**, **`Keep Working File`**, or **`Save Custom`**.

## Inspecting Conflicts

To list any unresolved conflicts in your repository:

```bash
tes conflicts
```

Pass `--json` to inspect the base, ours, and theirs snippets, `ast_union_preview`, `diagnostics`, and participating session IDs:

```bash
tes conflicts --json
```

## Resolving from the CLI

Resolve a conflicted file using one of five strategies:

```bash
# Combine both sides' AST declarations and statements in order
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy ast-union

# Keep the first session/branch's version
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy ours

# Keep the second session/branch's version
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy theirs

# Use the file as currently edited and saved on disk
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy working

# Write explicit resolved content inline or from a file
tes resolve src/App.vue --strategy content --content-file resolved-app.vue
```

## Checkpoints

Before asking an AI agent to perform a large multi-file refactor, save a named checkpoint:

```bash
tes checkpoint before-refactor
```

## Restoring Files

Use `tes restore` (or `tes reset`) to restore a branch or specific files to any checkpoint, commit SHA, `HEAD~N`, or branch:

```bash
# Restore the current branch to a named checkpoint or previous commit
tes restore before-refactor
tes restore HEAD~1

# Restore a specific branch without switching to it
tes restore -b feat/pricing HEAD~1

# Discard uncommitted changes in a specific file
tes restore src/App.vue

# Restore a file from another branch or commit
tes restore --source main src/App.vue
```

## Undo

Every claim, file reconciliation, checkpoint, restore, and merge is recorded in `.git/tessera`.

View recent operations:

```bash
tes oplog
```

Undo the most recent operation (including a merge):

```bash
tes undo
```

Or roll back to a specific operation ID from `tes oplog`:

```bash
tes undo --op <operation-id>
```

## See Also

- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Conflict resolver and branch graph
- [tes resolve](/cli/resolve) - CLI command reference
- [tes restore](/cli/restore) - CLI command reference

---

# Editor Support

The Tessera extension (`tessera-vscode.vsix`) works in **VS Code** and all **VS Code-based editors** (including **Antigravity**, **Cursor**, **Windsurf**, **Kiro**, and **VSCodium**), providing real-time branch switching, a 2D commit graph, active session monitoring, and one-click conflict resolution.

## Status Bar

When you open a repository initialized with `tes init`, two items appear on the left side of the status bar:

1. **Current Branch (`main`)**: Displays the branch currently checked out in your editor working tree. Click it at any time to switch your editor to another branch.
2. **`Graph` / `N Conflicts`**: Opens the Branch Graph. If any unresolved conflicts exist, this item highlights in red (`N Conflicts`) and opens the Conflict Resolver when clicked.

> **Note:** In workspaces that have not been initialized with `tes init`, the Tessera status bar items stay hidden automatically.

## Live Attribution

Whenever any active session has uncommitted edits in a file on your active editor branch (whether a single session or multiple concurrent agents), the extension highlights each session's lines in real time:

1. **Top-of-File CodeLenses**: Shows a **`Dismiss Highlights`** CodeLens whenever highlights are active, plus a file summary CodeLens at line 1 whenever two or more sessions are concurrently editing the file (`2 agents concurrently editing this file (main): antigravity-a1b2 · claude-c3d4`).
2. **Hunk CodeLens**: Appears directly above the start line of each session's modified section (`<agent_id> · L<start>-L<end>: <intent>`). For terminal and CLI sessions with a navigable terminal waypoint (`term-*`, TTY, `tmux`, `WezTerm`, `kitty`, `Terminal.app`, or `iTerm2`), the CodeLens appends a clickable **`· Jump to Terminal`** link that focuses that terminal tab or pane.
3. **Gutter Borders and Line Highlights**: Each session slot receives a distinct 3px left border and line highlight along with a matching marker on the scrollbar overview ruler (overlapping lines from multiple sessions use an error highlight).
4. **Inline Labels and Hover Cards**: The first line of each session's section displays an italic inline label (`<agent_id>: <intent>`), and hovering any highlighted line shows a card with the session ID, branch, line range, task intent, a **`Jump to Terminal`** link (when navigable), and a **`Branch Graph`** link.

```ts
// Live Multi-Agent Attribution in src/currency.ts (main):
// [CodeLens] 2 agents concurrently editing this file (main): antigravity-a1b2 · claude-c3d4
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  // [antigravity-a1b2 · L3-L6: Add locale and decimals]
  currency = "USD",
  locale = "en-US",
  decimals = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
// [claude-c3d4 · L10-L14: Add formatCompact helper]
export function formatCompact(cents: number) {
  return new Intl.NumberFormat("en-US", {
    style: "currency", currency: "USD", notation: "compact"
  }).format(cents / 100);
}
```

## Branch Graph

Click **`Graph`** in the status bar (or run **`Tessera: Open Branch Graph`** from the Command Palette) to open the 2D commit graph:

- **Branch Column Headers**: Sticky headers at the top of each branch lane show the branch name, **`Active`** / **`Switch`** status badge (clicking the header switches the editor working tree to that branch), a delete button (`×` on non-trunk branches), a **`Default`** or **`Branch`** badge, and the branch's assigned port (`:<port>`).
- **Topbar Actions**: Includes one-click buttons to **`Resolve Conflict`** (when conflicts exist), **`Merge into <trunk>`**, **`Collapse Linear`** / **`Expand All`**, and **`Refresh`**.
- **Newest-First Commit History**: Renders commit and merge cards newest-first so **`Working`** and **`HEAD`** nodes stay immediately visible beneath the sticky column headers. Consecutive commits with matching conventional topics group horizontally, long linear chains collapse into expandable pills, file chips open diffs or conflicted files, **`Working`** cards include a **`Discard`** button, and conflicted nodes are highlighted with a red border.

## Sidebar Views

Clicking the Tessera icon in the Activity Bar opens three sidebar views (plus a **Branches** view inside the Source Control sidebar):

### Branches
Lists every branch in the repository with its short commit SHA, active marker, port (`:<port>`), and modified file count ahead of `main`. Expanding a branch lets you:
- Switch your editor to that branch
- Open the branch's assigned dev server (`localhost:<port>`)
- Click any modified file (`M`) to open a side-by-side diff against `main`

### Sessions
Displays all active AI agent and terminal sessions (`antigravity-*`, `claude-*`, `codex-*`, `cursor-*`, `term-*`), their target branch, and their current task intent. Expanding a terminal session provides a **`Jump to Terminal`** action (and the inline **Jump to Session** button or `tes session focus <session-id>` focuses the session's terminal tab, multiplexer pane, or IDE window), along with branch switching, claimed symbols, and modified files.

### Conflicts & Checkpoints
Lists active conflicts, saved checkpoints (`tes checkpoint`), and stashes (`stash@{0}`, expandable to view stashed files with inline **Pop Stash** and **Drop Stash** actions), with toolbar actions to create a new checkpoint or open the Conflict Resolver.

## Conflict Resolution

When a merge conflict occurs:
1. The extension opens the conflicted file in your editor at the `<<<<<<<` conflict marker.
2. Resolve the conflict by editing the file and saving (`Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S` resolves once markers are removed) or by opening the **Conflict Resolver** panel (click **`N Conflicts`** in the status bar or run **`Tessera: Open Conflict Resolver`**).
3. Each conflict card displays competing agent intents, **`Verification Diagnostics`** (when `diagnostics` is present, such as from a failed `--verify` check), **`Base`** (when `base_snippet` is present), **`Ours`**, and **`Theirs`** snippets, an editable **`AST-Union Preview`** box, an **`Open in Editor`** button, and one-click actions: **`Accept AST-Union`**, **`Accept Ours`**, **`Accept Theirs`**, **`Keep Working File`**, and **`Save Custom`**.

## See Also

- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - How editor branches and terminal branches interact
- [Conflicts](/guides/conflict-resolution) - Resolving conflicts and rolling back changes

---

# Configuration

Tessera includes default settings for JavaScript/TypeScript, Rust, Python, Go, PHP, Ruby, Elixir, JVM, Swift, C/C++, Zig, .NET, and Dart projects.

You can customize ports, verification gates, Copy-on-Write cache directories, and environment variable templates using either a `tessera.toml` file in your project root or the `tes config` command.

## Quick Start

View the active configuration for your repository:

```bash
tes config show
```

## Configuration File (`tessera.toml`)

To share configuration across your team in version control, create a `tessera.toml` file in your repository root.

### Example Configuration

```toml
trunk_branch = "main"
base_port = 3000
port_stride = 100
port_isolation = true
auto_isolate_dirty_claims = true
watch_interval_ms = 75
watch_timeout_secs = 90

cow_cache_dirs = [
  "node_modules",
  ".pnpm-store",
  "target",
  ".venv",
  "venv",
  "vendor"
]

package_globs = [
  "crates/*",
  "packages/*",
  "apps/*",
  "services/*"
]

# Execution-sensitive fields below require `tes config trust`
verify_command = "npm run build"
pager = "less -FRX"

extra_bin_dirs = [
  ".venv/bin",
  "venv/bin",
  "node_modules/.bin",
  "vendor/bin"
]

[custom_env]
DATABASE_URL = "postgres://localhost:5432/app_slot_{slot}"
REDIS_URL = "redis://localhost:6379/{slot}"
VITE_PORT = "{port}"
```

## Configuration Options

### Declarative Settings (Loaded Automatically)

These settings are declarative and load automatically from `.git/tessera/config.toml` and any checked-in `tessera.toml`.

#### `trunk_branch`

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"main"`
- **Description:** Default primary branch for the repository.

```toml
trunk_branch = "main"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set trunk_branch main
```

#### `base_port`

- **Type:** `number`
- **Default:** `3000`
- **Description:** Starting port used when calculating isolated session ports (`PORT = base_port + slot * port_stride`). Must be `>= 1024` in `tessera.toml`.

```toml
base_port = 3000
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set base_port 3000
```

#### `port_stride`

- **Type:** `number`
- **Default:** `100`
- **Description:** Port increment between session slots (for example, Slot 1 receives `3100`, Slot 2 receives `3200`). Must be `>= 25` in `tessera.toml`.

```toml
port_stride = 100
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set port_stride 100
```

#### `port_isolation`

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Description:** When enabled (`true`) or when `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1` is set in the environment, `tes env` and `tes exec` automatically export `PORT` and framework port environment variables (`VITE_PORT`, `FLASK_RUN_PORT`, `UVICORN_PORT`, `RAILS_PORT`, and more) and prepend POSIX CLI port-wrapper shims (`TES_SHIM_BIN`) for each session slot.

```toml
port_isolation = true
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set port_isolation true
```

#### `auto_isolate_dirty_claims`

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `true`
- **Description:** When `true`, running `tes claim` without `--branch` on a file that already has uncommitted changes from the user or a peer session automatically isolates the new session onto `agent/<session_id>` instead of mixing edits into in-progress work. Pass `--branch <branch>` explicitly when same-branch collaboration is intended, or set this option to `false`.

```toml
auto_isolate_dirty_claims = true
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set auto_isolate_dirty_claims false
```

#### `watch_interval_ms`

- **Type:** `number`
- **Default:** `75`
- **Description:** Polling interval in milliseconds for the background write watcher started on `tes claim` (clamped to a minimum of `15` ms in `tessera.toml`).

```toml
watch_interval_ms = 75
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set watch_interval_ms 75
```

#### `watch_timeout_secs`

- **Type:** `number`
- **Default:** `90`
- **Description:** Idle timeout in seconds before the background write watcher exits automatically (clamped to a minimum of `5` seconds in `tessera.toml`).

```toml
watch_timeout_secs = 90
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set watch_timeout_secs 90
```

#### `co_author`

- **Type:** `boolean`
- **Default:** `false`
- **Description:** When enabled (`true`), appends a `Co-authored-by:` trailer (`Co-authored-by: Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>` by default) to commits created by Tessera (`tes commit`, `tes merge`, `tes resolve`, `tes pull`, and `tes cherry-pick`). Commits always record your active Git/system user as the primary `Author`.

```toml
co_author = true
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set co_author true
```

#### `co_author_trailer`

- **Type:** `string`
- **Default:** `"Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>"`
- **Description:** Custom identity used in the `Co-authored-by: <trailer>` line when `co_author = true`.

```toml
co_author = true
co_author_trailer = "Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set co_author_trailer "Tessera <noreply@tessera.getlunaris.dev>"
```

#### `cow_cache_dirs`

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `["target", "node_modules", ".pnpm-store", ".turbo", ".next", ".nuxt", ".svelte-kit", "dist", "build", ".venv", "venv", "__pycache__", ".pytest_cache", ".mypy_cache", ".ruff_cache", "vendor", "_build", "deps", ".gradle", ".build", ".zig-cache", "zig-out", ".dart_tool", "cmake-build-debug", "cmake-build-release"]`
- **Description:** Untracked dependency and build cache directories cloned via Copy-on-Write into every branch sandbox.

Add directories via CLI:

```bash
tes config add-cache-dir .nx .angular
```

#### `package_globs`

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `["crates/*", "packages/*", "apps/*", "services/*"]`
- **Description:** Monorepo workspace or package glob patterns scanned when discovering nested dependency caches.

Add package globs via CLI:

```bash
tes config add-package-glob "modules/*" "plugins/*"
```

### Trust-Gated Execution Settings

Because these settings influence executed commands, `PATH` resolution, or runtime environment variables, values defined in a checked-in `tessera.toml` are ignored until you explicitly run `tes config trust`. Local overrides set directly via `tes config` in `.git/tessera/config.toml` take effect immediately.

#### `verify_command`

- **Type:** `string | null`
- **Default:** `null`
- **Description:** Optional verification command executed when running `tes merge --verify` or `tes commit --verify` (and over MCP when `verify: true` is passed).

```toml
verify_command = "npm test"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set verify_command "npm test"
# or using the shorthand flag:
tes config --verify-cmd "npm test"
```

#### `pager`

- **Type:** `string | null`
- **Default:** `null` (falls back to `TES_PAGER` -> `GIT_PAGER` -> `git config core.pager` -> `PAGER` -> `less -FRX`)
- **Description:** Terminal pager command used for `tes diff`, `tes log`, `tes oplog`, `tes branch`, `tes stash list`, and any command invoked with `--paginate` when `stdout` is an interactive terminal. Set to `"cat"` or pass `-P` / `--no-pager` to disable paging.

```toml
pager = "less -FRX"
```

Update via CLI:

```bash
tes config set pager "delta --paging=always"
```

#### `extra_bin_dirs`

- **Type:** `string[]`
- **Default:** `[".venv/bin", "venv/bin", "node_modules/.bin", "vendor/bin"]`
- **Description:** Relative directories inside the branch sandbox prepended to `PATH` during `tes exec`. Generic project directories such as `bin` and `.bin` are excluded from the untrusted defaults for security so cloned repositories cannot shadow standard system utilities; add them explicitly via `tes config add-bin-dir` or a trusted `tessera.toml`.

Add binary directories via CLI:

```bash
tes config add-bin-dir scripts/bin tools/bin
```

#### `[custom_env]`

- **Type:** `table`
- **Default:** `{}`
- **Description:** Custom environment variable templates injected into `tes exec`. Supports `{slot}`, `{port}`, `{branch}`, and `{agent_id}` placeholders (interpolated in a single pass). Sensitive loader, shell, proxy, and toolchain injection keys (such as `LD_PRELOAD`, `DYLD_INSERT_LIBRARIES`, `COMSPEC`, `NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS`, `HTTP_PROXY`, and `SSH_AUTH_SOCK`) are rejected automatically.

```toml
[custom_env]
DATABASE_URL = "postgres://localhost:5432/app_test_{slot}"
APP_URL = "http://localhost:{port}"
```

Set environment templates via CLI:

```bash
tes config set-env DATABASE_URL "postgres://localhost:5432/app_test_{slot}"
tes config set-env APP_URL "http://localhost:{port}"
```

### Repository Trust (`tessera.toml`)

When cloning an external repository that includes a checked-in `tessera.toml`, declarative settings (`trunk_branch`, `base_port`, `port_stride`, `watch_interval_ms`, `watch_timeout_secs`, `auto_isolate_dirty_claims`, `co_author`, `co_author_trailer`, `port_isolation`, `cow_cache_dirs`, and `package_globs`) are loaded automatically.

To prevent untrusted repositories from executing arbitrary commands, shadowing binaries, or injecting environment variables automatically, `verify_command`, `pager`, `extra_bin_dirs`, and `custom_env` in `tessera.toml` are ignored until you explicitly trust the current file digest:

```bash
# trust the repository's current tessera.toml
tes config trust

# revoke trust for tessera.toml
tes config untrust
```

If `tessera.toml` changes later (for example, after a `tes pull`), its Blake3 digest changes and execution-sensitive fields remain inactive until you review the file and run `tes config trust` again.

## See Also

- [tes config](/cli/config) - CLI command reference
- [Sandboxes](/guides/running-tests-and-servers) - How branch sandboxes use cache directories and ports
- [Getting Started](/getting-started/) - Project initialization guide

# Examples

Step-by-step walkthroughs for working with multiple agents and branches in Tessera.

## Available Examples

- [Same-Branch Editing](/examples/same-branch) - Two agents editing the same function or file on `main`
- [Feature Branches](/examples/parallel-branches) - Building two features on separate branches and merging them into `main`
- [Conflict Resolution](/examples/conflict-resolution) - Handling incompatible edits on the same line using the editor or CLI

## Quick Examples

### Initialize and Configure Shell

```bash
tes init
tes env --install
```

### Switch Terminals to Different Branches

Enable `port_isolation` (defaults to `false`; or set `TES_PORT_ISOLATION=1`) when running dev servers side by side on separate branches:

```bash
tes config set port_isolation true

# Terminal 1
tes switch feat/pricing
npm run dev

# Terminal 2
tes switch feat/faq
npm run dev
```

### Merge Multiple Feature Branches into `main`

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

---

# Same-Branch Editing

This example walks through two agents editing the same function in `src/currency.ts` on `main`.

```text
[Workflow: Same-Branch AST Merging on main]
1. Prompt on main   -> Agent 1 ("Add locale") & Agent 2 ("Add decimals") target src/currency.ts
2. Concurrent Edits -> Both agents save directly on main (no file locks)
3. Tree-sitter AST  -> Parses FunctionDecl -> merges ParamNode[1] (locale) + ParamNode[2] (decimals)
4. Unified on Disk  -> Both edits preserved in src/currency.ts with zero overwrites
```

## Starting File

Suppose `src/currency.ts` on `main` contains:

```ts
export function formatCurrency(cents: number, currency: string = "USD"): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(2);
  return `${currency} ${amount}`;
}
```

## Prompting Two Agents

Open two AI agent tabs and give both a prompt that modifies `formatCurrency`:

- **Tab 1**: *"Add a `locale: string = 'en-US'` parameter to `formatCurrency` in `src/currency.ts`."*
- **Tab 2**: *"Add a `decimals: number = 2` parameter to `formatCurrency` in `src/currency.ts`."*

## How It Works

1. Both agents claim `src/currency.ts` against the same starting commit on `main` using `--branch main` (`tes claim --branch main --intent "..." src/currency.ts`).
2. Agent 1 writes its edit and runs `tes hook post-tool --path src/currency.ts`.
3. Agent 2 writes its edit and runs `tes hook post-tool --path src/currency.ts`.
4. Tessera parses the base version and both agents' versions using Tree-sitter and merges the parameter list and function body automatically.

> **Note:** Because `auto_isolate_dirty_claims` defaults to `true`, omitting `--branch` on `tes claim` when `src/currency.ts` already has uncommitted edits automatically isolates the second session onto `agent/<session_id>`. Passing `--branch main` explicitly opts into same-branch collaboration (or set `auto_isolate_dirty_claims = false` in `tessera.toml` / via `tes config set auto_isolate_dirty_claims false`).

## Merged Result

```ts
export function formatCurrency(
  cents: number,
  currency: string = "USD",
  locale: string = "en-US",
  decimals: number = 2
): string {
  const amount = (cents / 100).toFixed(decimals);
  return `[${locale}] ${currency} ${amount}`;
}
```

## Committing

Check the status and commit:

```bash
tes status
tes diff
tes commit -m "feat(currency): support locale and decimals parameters"
```

## Next Steps

- [Feature Branches](/examples/parallel-branches) - Isolate two features on separate branches
- [Conflict Resolution](/examples/conflict-resolution) - Handle overlapping edits to the same expression

---

# Feature Branches

This example shows two agents building separate features on `feat/pricing` and `feat/faq` while both modifying `src/App.vue` in the same checkout, then merging both branches into `main`.

```text
[Workflow: Parallel Agents in One Repository]
1. Prompt in One Repo (~/acme-web)
   ├─ Agent 1: "Add Pricing"
   └─ Agent 2: "Add FAQ"
       │
       ▼
2. Own Branches (Isolated in .git/tessera while .git/HEAD stays on main)
   ├─ feat/pricing (Agent 1 · +Pricing)
   └─ feat/faq     (Agent 2 · +FAQ)
       │
       ▼
3. Branch Dev Servers (Copy-on-Write node_modules / target)
   ├─ http://localhost:3100 (feat/pricing)
   └─ http://localhost:3200 (feat/faq)
       │
       ▼
4. Merge into main (3-Way Tree-sitter AST Merge)
   └─ tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing and faq"
```

## Starting File

Suppose `src/App.vue` on `main` starts as:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import HelloWorld from './components/HelloWorld.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <HelloWorld />
</template>
```

## 1. Launch Two Agents on Separate Branches

Open two AI agent chat tabs in your editor:

- **Tab 1 (`feat/pricing`)**:
  > *"On branch `feat/pricing`, create `src/components/PricingCalculator.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*

- **Tab 2 (`feat/faq`)**:
  > *"On branch `feat/faq`, create `src/components/TestimonialsFaq.vue`, add it to `src/App.vue`, and verify with `npm run build`."*

## 2. Branch Isolation

Even though both agents edit `src/App.vue` in the same folder at the same time:

- `feat/pricing` only contains `HelloWorld.vue` and `PricingCalculator.vue`.
- `feat/faq` only contains `HelloWorld.vue` and `TestimonialsFaq.vue`.
- When each agent runs `tes exec -- npm run build`, the build runs inside that branch's Copy-on-Write sandbox (`branches/feat-pricing` and `branches/feat-faq`), so neither branch fails with missing-component errors.

## 3. Preview Either Branch

You can inspect the diff of each branch or switch your editor to preview it:

```bash
# Compare each branch against main
tes diff -b feat/pricing
tes diff -b feat/faq

# Or switch your editor working tree to feat/pricing
tes switch feat/pricing --editor
```

## 4. Merge Both Branches into `main`

Combine both branches into `main` with a single command:

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: add pricing calculator and testimonials faq"
```

Tessera merges both `<script setup>` import blocks and both `<template>` usages cleanly into `main`:

```vue
<script setup lang="ts">
import HelloWorld from './components/HelloWorld.vue'
import PricingCalculator from './components/PricingCalculator.vue'
import TestimonialsFaq from './components/TestimonialsFaq.vue'
</script>

<template>
  <HelloWorld />
  <PricingCalculator />
  <TestimonialsFaq />
</template>
```

## Next Steps

- [Conflict Resolution](/examples/conflict-resolution) - See what happens when two branches change the exact same line
- [Branches](/guides/branches-and-terminals) - Learn more about branch management

---

# Conflict Resolution

This example shows what happens when two branches modify the exact same line in incompatible ways, and how to resolve the conflict in your editor or from the CLI.

## 1. Creating a Conflict

Suppose `index.html` on `main` has:

```html
<title>My App</title>
```

Now suppose:
- Branch `feat/pricing` changes `<title>` to `<title>Pricing | My App</title>`.
- Branch `feat/faq` changes `<title>` to `<title>FAQ | My App</title>`.

When you merge both branches into `main`:

```bash
tes merge feat/pricing feat/faq --into main -m "feat: merge pricing and faq"
```

All non-overlapping files and components merge automatically, and Tessera reports `1` conflict on `index.html`.

## 2. Resolving in Your Editor

If you have the Tessera IDE extension installed (in VS Code or any VS Code-based editor):

1. `index.html` opens in your editor at the `<<<<<<<` line:
   ```html
   <<<<<<< ours
   <title>Pricing | My App</title>
   =======
   <title>FAQ | My App</title>
   >>>>>>> theirs
   ```
2. Edit the line to what you want:
   ```html
   <title>My App | Pricing and FAQ</title>
   ```
3. Save the file (`Cmd+S` / `Ctrl+S`). The extension detects that the conflict markers have been removed and resolves the conflict automatically.

## 3. Resolving from the CLI

You can also inspect and resolve conflicts directly from your terminal:

```bash
# List active conflicts
tes conflicts

# Resolve using the edited file on disk
tes resolve index.html --strategy working

# Or pick one side directly
tes resolve index.html --strategy ours
tes resolve index.html --strategy theirs
```

## Next Steps

- [Conflicts](/guides/conflict-resolution) - Learn about checkpoints, `tes restore`, and `tes undo`
- [Editor Support](/guides/ide-extension) - Explore the Conflict Resolver panel
